_notes.howToUse: Set custom project metadata by repo, slug, or human-readable title. Use titles when you want a stable manual label for a synced repository. Useful fields include title, subtitle, status, startDate, endDate, lessonsLearned, pending, statusNote, tags, tech, contributorsWanted, cardEmoji, previewImage, images, and links.

fieldGuide.title: Manual display title for the project.
fieldGuide.subtitle: Short subtitle shown below the project title.
fieldGuide.checklist: Keyed object of checklist entries with status (done, inprogress, or todo) and title.
fieldGuide.status: One of the allowed status values below.
fieldGuide.statusNote: Small note shown on project cards and project pages.
fieldGuide.startDate: Exact date or semester label such as Fall 2026, Summer 2026, or Winter 2027; used for timeline ordering.
fieldGuide.endDate: Optional exact date or semester label for completion or pause. Use current or present for ongoing work.
fieldGuide.lessonsLearned: Short description of the skills or technical lessons learned.
fieldGuide.pending: Short description of the next milestone or unfinished work.
fieldGuide.cardEmoji: Emoji shown before the project title.
fieldGuide.hackathonName: Name of the hackathon/event the project came from.
fieldGuide.hackathonUrl: Optional link to the event page.
fieldGuide.replacementLabel: Label for the newer project replacing an archived one, like Omnibot.
fieldGuide.replacementUrl: Link for the replacement project, like /projects/omnibot or /projects#omnibot.
fieldGuide.buildsOnLabels: Labels for older/related projects a newer one is building off of.
fieldGuide.buildsOnUrls: Links paired with buildsOnLabels, usually project slugs like /projects/battlebots.
fieldGuide.forkedFrom: Original project/repo name if this is a fork.
fieldGuide.images: Extra image URLs for the project.
fieldGuide.links: Object with github, homepage, demo, schematic, bom, and/or designFiles URLs.
